page: Microsoft Azure E32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem features 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside comprehensive hardware support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, AES cryptography, and AMD SVM virtualization running under Microsoft Hyper-V.

Memory capacity is configured at 256.0 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio suitable for memory-intensive enterprise environments. Storage includes 1890 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, providing low-latency ephemeral scratch space alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include discrete GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression achieving top-tier ranks within the upper 10 percent of tested cloud instances. Multi-core compute performance sits in the middle tiers, delivering a PassMark CPU score of 57,284.51 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 59,927.61. In memory and caching metrics, PassMark memory benchmarking reached strong top-quartile results with uncached read throughput of 101.24 GB/sec and uncached write throughput of 67.55 GB/sec.

Application testing reveals steady throughput for caching and operational data stores, achieving 49.9 million Redis SET operations per second and 41.99 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. While small-scale language model inference exhibits rapid execution on CPU vector extensions, throughput drops steeply when handling 70B parameter models down to 2.46 tokens per second, indicating that large AI workloads require dedicated accelerators.

Cost efficiency is centered around the generous memory-to-core ratio and direct integration of high-capacity local NVMe storage, removing the need for external disks in temporary data pipelines. Microsoft Azure E32ads_v7 is suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, relational database hosting, batch compression pipelines, and memory-bound enterprise data processing.

The system incorporates 256.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio, and bundles 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, but lacks discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong overall memory bandwidth, alongside steady database operation rates and 49.9 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-bound large model inference exhibits substantial latency relative to GPU alternatives. Cost efficiency is balanced across dense memory provisioning and bundled local NVMe storage, making the instance an effective platform for in-memory databases, relational caching platforms, ETL batch pipelines, and memory-intensive analytics.
